title: Safaricom profit jumps 36% as M-PESA revenue passes KSh 100 billion
dek: Kenyans moved KSh 23.5 trillion through M-PESA in six months, and Fuliza borrowing nearly doubled.
body: Safaricom has reported a group net profit of KSh 58.2 billion for the six months to September 2026, up 35.9% from KSh 42.8 billion a year earlier.
M-PESA remained the engine. Its revenue rose 13.6% to KSh 100.1 billion, the first time the half year figure has crossed the KSh 100 billion mark.

body.h: What the numbers say about how Kenyans use money

list: 27.4 billion M-PESA transactions in six months, up 25.2%
KSh 23.56 trillion moved through the platform, up 16.6%
Fuliza overdrafts of KSh 1.16 trillion, up 84%
Average data price down to about KSh 51.50 per GB, from about KSh 57.75

body: The Fuliza figure stands out. Borrowing on the overdraft service grew far faster than the money moved on M-PESA itself, a sign that many households are leaning on short term credit to get through the month.
Ethiopia, Safaricom's newer market, is still losing money, but the losses narrowed sharply. The company did not announce an interim dividend.

Cheaper data per gigabyte is good news for heavy users, but Fuliza fees add up quickly when the overdraft becomes a habit rather than an emergency tool. Checking your Fuliza limit and repayment dates on the M-PESA menu is a simple way to stay in control.
